---
title: Publish a result
description: Turn a completed local simulation into a useful research page.
---

Each case study should let a visitor understand the question, inspect the result and find the exact material needed to reproduce it.

## Use a consistent page structure

1. **Question:** what changes and what is held fixed?
2. **Scene:** geometry, dimensions, materials, TX/RX placement and motion.
3. **Method:** software versions, solver settings, enabled interactions and assumptions.
4. **Result:** one clear figure or video, followed by numerical evidence with units.
5. **Limits:** what was approximated, omitted or not validated?
6. **Reproduce:** a versioned code reference, scene/data download and run instructions.

## Put each file in the right place

| Material | Suggested destination |
|---|---|
| Explanations and tutorial steps | Quarto `.qmd` pages in this website |
| Compact figures and short preview clips | `assets/` in this website |
| Full Blender movies and conference recordings | YouTube embeds with direct links |
| Source code and issue tracking | The relevant GitHub software repository |
| Large `.blend` scenes and packaged examples | Versioned GitHub Release assets |
| Archived datasets supporting a paper | A published repository such as Zenodo, with a verified DOI |
| Lightweight interactive result viewers | Static HTML/JavaScript plus compact exported data |

Keep the website source in its own folder. Publish selected outputs from the working projects, rather than making the entire Codex working directory a website.

## Add a new page

Create `examples/my-study.qmd` and use this outline:

````markdown
---
title: "A descriptive study title"
description: "The question and the main comparison."
---

## Question
State the comparison and the controlled variables.

## Method
Record the exact scene, versions and settings.

## Results
![Describe the quantity and units](../assets/my-study.webp)

## Limitations
State the boundaries of the evidence.

## Reproduce
Link to a versioned release and its instructions.
````

Add the page to the `website.sidebar.contents` list in `_quarto.yml` and link it from `examples/index.qmd`. The existing `examples/*.qmd` render pattern includes it in the build.

## Preview and publish

Install [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) and run these commands from the website folder:

```powershell
quarto preview
quarto render
```

Preview while editing; render before pushing. The included GitHub Actions workflow renders and deploys changes pushed to `main` after GitHub Pages is configured to use **GitHub Actions**. Pull requests build without deploying.

GitHub Pages serves the generated website. GPU simulations and Python workers run separately; this site’s build has code execution disabled. See [Quarto publishing](https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html) and [GitHub custom workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/using-custom-workflows-with-github-pages).
